question.text: A put option with strike Rs 180 and premium Rs 8 breaks even when the market price at expiry is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Put breakeven = Strike minus Premium = 180 minus 8 = Rs 172. At Rs 172 the intrinsic value of the put (180 minus 172 = Rs 8) exactly offsets the Rs 8 premium paid, so the buyer breaks even. The Trap: Rs 180 is the strike itself, where the put is at-the-money. Rs 188 (strike plus premium) is the call-style breakeven, not the put. Rs 164 (strike minus twice the premium) double-counts the premium. The correct rule for a long put is strike minus premium. Note: The previously duplicate "Rs 188" distractor at option D was replaced with Rs 164 so the four options are now distinct with exactly one correct answer (Rs 172). The unsupported Cross-Exam Context and Pro-Tip paragraphs were removed.
